translations.seg-0001: Hey, have you been working on some app lately? I keep seeing you post about it.
translations.seg-0002: Yeah! It's called Pebble, a Chinese learning tool that transcribes podcasts and translates them into English.
translations.seg-0003: That's pretty cool. What made you suddenly want to build this?
translations.seg-0004: It's really just solving my own pain point. I usually listen to podcasts on Xiaoyuzhou to learn Chinese, but there's no translation feature in the app at all, so I literally can't learn from it.
translations.seg-0005: I get it. That blocker is genuinely suffocating. So what's your Chinese level now?
translations.seg-0006: I'm currently preparing for HSK 5, and I want to learn through lots of input, like podcasts. But when there's something I can't understand, I can't look it up or note it down. I'm just stuck.
translations.seg-0007: So you just went ahead and built one yourself?
translations.seg-0008: Yeah, at first it was just for personal use. When you're a designer, your first reaction to a problem is — well, let me design a solution.
translations.seg-0009: That's amazing. That's literally eating your own dog food. So what exactly can Pebble do?
translations.seg-0010: It can transcribe your own podcast audio, translate it line by line into English, and show both side by side. That way I can listen and learn at the same time.
translations.seg-0011: Sounds really practical. So what's your mission?
translations.seg-0012: It's to let Chinese learners learn directly from real podcast content. Authentic, unfiltered material that's way better than textbooks.
translations.seg-0013: Nice nice, then you have to hook me up with one.
translations.seg-0014: Haha, just wait until I launch.
